text:
incident-bot: 🔔 SLO alert: realtime.p99 > 4.5s for us-east-1 streaming-route. triggered at 2026-03-17T14:02:08Z. Alert link: https://dashboard.internal/alerts/7943218888

mike-oncall: saw it, paging myself. starting triage. @sara-dev any recent rollouts? :eyes:

sara-dev: small config change to routing weights landed ~13:55 UTC (canary). noticed slight bump in p95 in canary but turned green after 10m. rolling to 100% at 13:58 UTC — could be related.

jordan-sre: checking kvcache hit-rate + pod latency. pulling quick graphs...

jordan-sre: dashboard snapshot: p99 spike aligns with increased kv-cache-miss-rate and a rise in worker RT calls. metrics: kvcache_miss_rate from 4% -> 28% at 13:59.

ops-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T13:58:40 by sara-dev -> service/realtime-routing v2.3.7, canary->prod progression automated.

mike-oncall: ok mark as potentially rollout-related. mitigation checklist: 1) pause rollout / rollback, 2) shift traffic to fallback region, 3) enable degraded routing (lower batching), 4) notify CS. Who can pause rollback now?

sara-dev: I can pause the rollout, doing that now: `kubectl patch deploy realtime-routing -p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'`

sara-dev: paused. confirming prod replicas still on v2.3.7 but no further canary progression.

jordan-sre: starting traffic shift to fallback variant on edge for us-east-1 (route -> streaming-compat-quant). Command: `./routectl shift --route streaming-route --to fallback --region us-east-1 --weight 100 --reason p99-spike`

ops-bot: routing change applied (ID: rt-794321). Noise may persist for ~30s while caches warm.

leo-eng: quick sanity check on infra: no autoscaler thrash, no recent node reboots. CPU ~55%, GPU utilization stable.

emily-cs: we have one customer (acme-inc) reporting delays in comp-srv feature at 14:00 UTC via support ticket #94321. CS alerted them that we're investigating.

mike-oncall: thanks. set customer impact = "degraded" for now. notify top 5 customers in the incident template.

jordan-sre: logs excerpt around 13:59 (filtered):
```
2026-03-17T13:59:03Z worker=stream-12 trace=abc123 latency=4789ms kv_hit=false model_call=ok
2026-03-17T13:59:04Z worker=stream-08 trace=def456 latency=5210ms kv_hit=false model_call=ok
2026-03-17T13:59:05Z worker=stream-12 trace=ghi789 latency=4901ms kv_hit=false model_call=ok
```

sara-dev: those kv misses line up with a config that accidentally disabled the prefix cache for streaming-route in v2.3.7. Investigating why canary didn't catch it in local tests.

mike-oncall: immediate action: keep rollout paused, keep fallback route in place, and disable batching for streaming-route to reduce tail amplification. Sara, can you toggle batching flag?

sara-dev: toggling batching to off: `POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/routes/streaming-route/config` payload `{ "batching": false }` -> response 202.

ops-bot: config change accepted. note: this will increase token cost but reduce tail latency.

jordan-sre: monitoring p99 now... initial trend: p99 falling from 5.2s -> 2.1s after route shift + batching off (first 45s). still watching kv warm-up.

mike-oncall: great. start an incident page with status = investigating, severity = medium, customer impact = degraded. I'll own oncall. Jordan/Sara please add postmortem placeholders (timeline + root-cause hypothesis: cache-config skipped).

emily-cs: notifying impacted customer list and setting expectation: 45-60m ETA for full mitigation.

leo-eng: note for later: add tighter canary gating for cache config changes (require canary traffic >5k qps or kv-hit smoke test).

sara-dev: ack — will open a follow-up PR for a canary smoke test and add a rollback hook.

jordan-sre: leaving quick checklist: 1) confirm p99 stabilized <2.5s for 5 consecutive minutes, 2) capture metrics+logs for 15m window, 3) coordinate rollback if stabilization fails.

mike-oncall: will run war room if p99 >3s persists for 10m. for now, monitoring. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: ⚠️ Update: p99 back to ~1.9s (14:04:20Z). Incident remains open for verification and postmortem.

mike-oncall: closing initial triage window, handing to SRE for follow-up. thanks team.

jordan-sre: taking postmortem action items. adding timeline and attaching logs.

sara-dev: adding PR link for canary smoke test: https://git.internal/r/realtime-routing/pull/482

emily-cs: updated support ticket and notified acme-inc primary contact.

mike-oncall: end of thread for initial triage. will reopen if regressions recur.
